shared_elements: carved stone in the round / freestanding stone sculpture
paired circular or ring-shaped motifs arranged symmetrically about a vertical axis
low-relief carving on a broad, flat-backed block
curved arc or crescent bands framing the discs
tapering columnar body below the decorated upper zone
pitted, weathered dark volcanic-looking stone surface
justification: Both show a vertically oriented stone mass whose upper zone carries two large paired circles/rings set symmetrically about a central axis, with arcing bands curving around them and a plainer tapering body beneath — a fairly specific correspondence rather than a generic one. The biggest differences are scale and finish: B is a complete, crisply incised monumental figure with a head, collar and belt-like band, while A is a small, heavily eroded fragment photographed close-up whose forms are coarse, bulbous and largely dissolved by weathering, so the shared scheme could be coincidental.
